supplement.holds: p. 12, Data Availability, describes datasets and materials; p. 20 lists DataSPSS.sav and researchtools.pdf, without specifying their contents or statistics. Neither file is embedded in this PDF. Finalization requests for both direct links and the DOI fallback failed with WinError 10013; contents remain unverified. No matching local supplement was found in the creativity literature or screening folders. The main PDF does not print outcome SDs or per-arm counts after model-specific exclusions.

paper_design_summary: Undergraduates at Yangzhou University were randomly assigned to AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel, or Human-only conditions for two stages of narrative writing; 112 students were analyzed for demographics after initial attrition/non-compliance screening, before further model-specific exclusions (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 7-9, Sections 2.5-3.3). Ten trained student raters and DeepSeek-V3 scored the narratives, and the final-draft analyses adjusted for first-draft scores and participant covariates (pp. 5-9, Sections 2.3-3.4). AI-first final drafts were written independently after an AI-assisted first draft, while AI-follow and AI-parallel final drafts were written with AI available (pp. 6-7, Section 2.4).

studies.label: Randomized two-stage narrative-writing experiment; experimental setting not stated

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individuals were assigned to AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel, or Human-only. The assigned mode determines AI access at each writing stage; assignment is between groups with repeated draft measurements.

assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration is stated in the complete document; p. 4 describes an exploratory approach.

arms.name: AI-first
arms.description: First draft written with generative AI (human-AI collaboration), final draft written independently; participants could reference but not modify their first draft (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The analyzed valid-case sample before model-specific influential-case exclusions contained 28 people in this arm (p. 4, Section 2.1). The post-exclusion arm count for each final-draft model is not reported, so n_analyzed is null.

arms.name: AI-follow
arms.description: First draft written independently, final draft written with generative AI (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The analyzed valid-case sample before model-specific influential-case exclusions contained 25 people in this arm (p. 4, Section 2.1). The post-exclusion arm count for each final-draft model is not reported, so n_analyzed is null.

arms.name: AI-parallel
arms.description: Both drafts written with generative AI (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The analyzed valid-case sample before model-specific influential-case exclusions contained 30 people in this arm (p. 4, Section 2.1). The post-exclusion arm count for each final-draft model is not reported, so n_analyzed is null.

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Both drafts written independently without any AI tools (control) (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The analyzed valid-case sample before model-specific influential-case exclusions contained 29 people in this arm (p. 4, Section 2.1). The post-exclusion arm count for each final-draft model is not reported, so n_analyzed is null.

participants.exclusions: p. 4, Section 2.1 reports 112 valid cases after screening for attrition and non-compliance; the original randomized total and initial losses by arm are not reported. The demographic analyses use N = 112 (p. 8, Section 3.1). p. 7, Section 2.5 reports missing values for five participants (4.5%) and five MICE datasets, retaining N = 112 before model-specific exclusions using Cook's Distance (D > 4/n). The human-rated overall-creativity model excludes seven influential cases (p. 8, Section 3.2), and the AI-rated model excludes eight (p. 9, Section 3.3). Neither overall model's post-exclusion total nor its post-exclusion per-arm counts are explicitly printed. The structured study and arm n_analyzed fields are therefore null; the 112-person sample and valid-case arm counts must not supply final-draft analysis denominators. No post-exclusion totals are calculated here. The reported sample and exclusions establish that each overall-creativity model analyzed more than 50 people. Section 3.4 gives no exclusion counts for subdomain models. The self-efficacy analysis excludes 10 cases and explicitly reports N = 102 analyzed (p. 9, Section 3.5).
participants.who: Undergraduates from Yangzhou University across humanities, social sciences, STEM, agriculture, and medicine; recruited in December 2024; required to have no reported language or writing impairments and experience using GenAI tools; performance-based compensation 25 to 45 CNY (p. 4, Section 2.1). Mean age 19.47 years (SD = 1.20; p. 8, Section 3.1).
participants.quote: Following data screening for attrition and non-compliance, 112 valid cases remained, resulting in a total of 224 creative writing samples (first and final drafts combined).
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 2.1; p. 7, Section 2.5; pp. 8-9, Sections 3.1-3.5

ai_tool.name_model: Participant-selected generative AI tools, with ChatGPT and DeepSeek as examples; tool versions and the distribution of tools used are not reported.
ai_tool.how_used: Participants chose their preferred AI tools, prompted freely, and could adopt or reject generated content during assigned AI-assisted stages (p. 7, Section 2.4; instructions on p. 5, Section 2.2.1). Interaction modes were not controlled or categorized (p. 11, Discussion). DeepSeek-V3 was an evaluator, not a standardized treatment tool (p. 6, Section 2.3.2).

task.description: Write a first and a final narrative draft on "Imagine and depict the future world". Instructions emphasized novelty, idea richness, diverse perspectives, descriptive detail, coherence, and completeness (pp. 4-5, Section 2.2.1). Participants could reference the first draft during the final stage but could not modify it directly (p. 7, Section 2.4).
task.duration: 15 minutes per stage, first draft and final draft (p. 6, Section 2.4); no separate follow-up session or interstage interval is reported.

outcomes.name: Final-draft overall narrative creativity (AI available during final drafting)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each narrative was scored by ten trained undergraduate raters who were blind to condition, using four 9-point dimensions (pp. 5-6, Sections 2.3-2.3.1). Calibration used 15 narratives; formal-evaluation ICC = 0.722, 95% CI [0.48, 0.88], using a two-way mixed model with absolute agreement and average measures (p. 6). The combination of raters and dimensions into overall creativity is not specified. The final-draft ANCOVA adjusts for first-draft score, age, gender, AI literacy, and creative personality (pp. 7-8, Section 2.5), excluding seven influential cases (p. 8, Section 3.2). Robustness variant, retained within this outcome under form-spec rule 7: DeepSeek-V3 ratings analyzed with the same covariates after excluding eight influential cases (p. 9, Section 3.3). DeepSeek-V3 test-retest r = .547 over one week and final-draft correlation with human scores r = .501 (p. 6, Section 2.3.2). That interval concerns repeated scoring, not delayed participant output. The standardizer used for reported Cohen's d is not specified. The 112-person valid-case sample and its arm counts precede these model-specific exclusions and must not be used as denominators for these final-draft estimates; exact printed post-exclusion totals and arm counts are unavailable.

contrasts.reported: Human ratings: Omnibus F(3, 96) = 9.62, p < .001, partial eta-squared (η²ₚ) = .38. Adjusted means: Human-only M = 5.65, SE = 0.10; AI-follow M = 4.81, SE = 0.10; p < .001, d = -1.41. DeepSeek-V3 robustness ratings: Omnibus F(3, 95) = 6.12, p < .001, partial eta-squared (η²ₚ) = .16. Human-only M = 6.40, SE = 0.20; AI-follow M = 5.61, SE = 0.20; p = .017, d = -0.70. Means are adjusted; SEs are standard errors, not SDs.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were explicitly randomly assigned to three generative-AI access patterns or a Human-only control (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The paper reports 112 people analyzed for demographics after initial screening and imputation, followed by seven influential-case exclusions from human-rated overall creativity and eight from the AI-rated robustness model; each overall-creativity model remains above the 50-person threshold (p. 4, Section 2.1; pp. 7-9, Sections 2.5-3.3). Exact post-exclusion totals are not separately printed and arm allocations of the exclusions are unknown, so structured n_analyzed fields are null and no derived totals are entered. Creativity is scored on participants' narratives by blind human raters and DeepSeek-V3 (pp. 5-7, Sections 2.3-2.4). AI-follow and AI-parallel final drafts answer with_ai; AI-first final drafts answer after_ai because that stage is independent, although the AI-assisted first draft remains available for reference (pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). The lab/online/field subtype remains unreported, recorded as design_class other; random assignment and all three eligibility criteria are established.

one_line_finding: Human-rated adjusted final-draft creativity was lower for AI-first (M = 4.86, d = -0.95, p = .002) and AI-follow (M = 4.81, d = -1.41, p < .001) than Human-only (M = 5.65), with no clear difference for AI-parallel (M = 5.17, d = -0.33, p = .262; p. 8, Section 3.2).
open_questions: The document does not explicitly state the study country or whether sessions occurred in a supervised laboratory, online, or in ordinary coursework; country is null and the randomized setting subtype remains unresolved.
Section 3.4 does not identify whether its numerical subdomain ANCOVAs use human or AI ratings. Both versions are plotted, so the measure for those numerical outcomes is null.

Original randomized counts and initial losses by arm are not reported. Final-draft overall-model totals after influential-case exclusions are not separately printed, per-arm allocations of those exclusions are unknown, and subdomain exclusion counts are not stated. Study and arm n_analyzed fields are null; the reported 112-person pool and seven/eight overall-model exclusions nevertheless settle the 50-person eligibility threshold.

Both people-lens problems were corrected: study and arm n_analyzed fields are null because the reported valid-case counts precede model-specific exclusions and final denominators are not explicitly printed. Reported counts are preserved with their scope in prose. All open questions and unresolved reconciliation differences are assessed in final.open_items; none prevents eligibility. The reconciliation object is retained unchanged as historical review evidence; its earlier count-field values are superseded by these final corrections. No effect sizes, sample totals, or arm statistics were calculated during finalization. Reconciliation completed 2026-10-09. Both raw forms parsed. All 375 markdown lines, including references, figures and the supplementary-file list, were read. Retained numbers were checked against PDF text; figure panels were inspected without estimating values. No new effect sizes, sample totals, or arm statistics were calculated. The 112 and arm counts are valid-case sample counts before model-specific exclusions, not counts randomized. The PDF text layer explicitly encodes η²ₚ in Sections 3.2 and 3.3; the markdown conversion and visual font render the subscript poorly. The eight final-draft subdomain measure fields are deliberately null because Section 3.4 does not identify the rater. Automated versions are robustness variants, consolidated under form-spec rule 7: raw S1-O3 is retained within S1-O1, raw S1-O4 within S1-O2, and raw S1-O14 within S1-O13. New S1-O15 through S1-O18 retain first-draft subdomains shown in Figures 3 and 4 but omitted by both screeners. This gives 15 outcome entries and retains every output-scored construct and stage; no outcome family is omitted. Outcome IDs otherwise preserve the raw-form IDs. Human final-draft overall creativity is the paper's main analysis (Section 3.2); no first-draft primary designation is stated. Among with_ai contrasts, AI-parallel is the arm closest to continuous free chatbot access under codebook Section 8. AI-first final drafts are immediate revisions with the earlier AI-assisted text available; they are not a delayed transfer task. No across-people similarity/diversity measure is reported; flexibility concerns categories within narratives. Creative self-efficacy is excluded as self-report; its reported ANCOVA is F(3, 93) = 2.29, p = .083, with N = 102 after 10 exclusions (p. 9, Section 3.5). The reported post hoc power is .844 using two covariates (p. 4, Section 2.1), whereas the fitted model adjusts for first-draft score plus age, gender, AI literacy, and creative personality (p. 8, Section 2.5); this difference is retained without correction. No sample overlap or preregistration is stated. Differences only in synonymous labels, repeated details already elsewhere in both forms, or additional locators for the same evidence are not counted.

open_items.item: Study country is not explicitly stated (open_questions[0]; unresolved reconciliation difference for participants.country; p. 4, Section 2.1). Author confirmation would settle the location; no eligibility criterion depends on country.

The laboratory, online or coursework setting is not stated (open_questions[0]; unresolved reconciliation difference for design_class; pp. 4-7, Methods). Authors could confirm the RCT subtype. This does not unsettle criterion 1 because individual random assignment to AI-access schedules is explicit.

The evaluator behind the numerical subdomain ANCOVAs is unspecified (open_questions[1]; unresolved reconciliation difference for S1-O5 through S1-O12.measure; p. 9, Section 3.4; pp. 18-19, Figures 3-4). Author identification of the score source would settle attribution. Either evaluator scores participants' narratives, and overall human-rated creativity independently establishes criterion 3.

Original randomized totals, randomized arm counts and initial attrition/non-compliance losses by arm are unreported (open_questions[2]; p. 4, Section 2.1). Authors could provide the participant flow. These details affect attrition assessment; random assignment and more than 50 analyzed people are already established.

Post-exclusion totals and per-arm counts for the creativity models are not explicitly printed; subdomain exclusion counts are also absent (open_questions[2]; pp. 7-9, Sections 2.5 and 3.2-3.4). Participant data with model-specific exclusion indicators would settle the denominators; the linked DataSPSS.sav contents remain unverified. The reported pool and overall-model exclusions already settle criterion 2.

Final-draft ANCOVAs adjust for first-draft scores already exposed to AI in AI-first and AI-parallel; numerical unadjusted final-draft contrasts are absent (open_questions[3]; pp. 6-8, Sections 2.4-2.5). Participant-level scores and allocation data would permit checking unadjusted contrasts. This affects effect interpretation, not the three screening criteria.

Aggregation of dimensions and raters into overall creativity is unspecified (open_questions[4]; pp. 5-6, Sections 2.3-2.3.1). An explicit scoring protocol is needed; researchtools.pdf is linked but its contents are unverified. This concerns measurement details, while criterion 3 is already met by scoring the narratives.

The standardizer used for reported Cohen's d is unspecified (open_questions[4]; pp. 8-9, Sections 3.2-3.4). Authors could identify the calculation. This affects effect-size interpretation and extraction, not eligibility.

Supplement contents remain unverified because both direct file requests and the DOI fallback failed with WinError 10013 (open_questions[5]; p. 12, Data Availability; p. 20, Supplementary Files). Access to the linked files would establish what materials and statistics they contain. The saved main PDF establishes all three eligibility criteria without them.
